outcome: Apgar level less than five at five minutes
Gross motor function classification (level III-V) impairment
cohort: Participants were children with dyskinetic or bilateral spastic cerebral palsy, born in Denmark between 1999 and 2007, and registered in the Danish nationwide CP register.
finding: Children with dyskinetic cerebral palsy experienced more peri- or neonatal adverse events and had more severe neurodevelopmental impairment compared to those with bilateral spastic cerebral palsy, despite some overlapping clinical features.
